title: GitHub Actions job permissions shorthand (.github/policy.rego): job-level permissions: read-all or write-all is denied, so list explicit scopes
answers: Why does my workflow fail the policy check when a job has permissions: write-all?
Which job-level permissions values does the GitHub Actions policy accept?
Where is the check that rejects read-all or write-all job permissions implemented?
Does the policy still accept permissions: {} or object-form permissions on a job?
body:
Path: .github/policy.rego:deny_job_permissions_shorthand checks each job in input.jobs of workflow YAML under .github/workflows (run by Conftest) for a job-level `permissions` value equal to the shorthand string `read-all` or `write-all`, such as `build: permissions: write-all`.
Rule: Job-level permissions must be the explicit scope map (for example `contents: read`) rather than the shorthand strings. The denial message names the job id and the shorthand value and asks the author to list the scopes the job actually needs. Fix it by replacing the shorthand with the specific scope keys; top-level permissions is a separate check (deny_top_level_permissions) that requires exactly {}.
Symptom: A job could set `permissions: write-all` and still pass the policy, because the earlier job-level check only verified that a permissions key was present.
Constraints: Matches only the two exact strings. Object-form permissions and the empty object are not flagged by this rule (the empty object is handled by the separate redundant-permissions rule). Only jobs are evaluated, so composite action.yml files are not checked by it.
Applies: Workflow YAML under .github/workflows checked by Conftest with .github/policy.rego; covers job-level permissions shorthand only.
applies: Workflow job-level permissions in .github/workflows checked by .github/policy.rego; not top-level permissions and not composite actions.
says: Why does my workflow fail the policy check when a job uses write-all permissions?
Conftest rejects read-all or write-all on a job; which permissions format is accepted?
The policy wants explicit permission scopes on each job instead of a blanket shorthand
Can I still use an empty permissions object or a scope map on a job without the check complaining?
search: GitHub Actions job-level permissions shorthand policy: job permissions set to the exact strings read-all or write-all are denied, and the fix is listing explicit scopes. Only the two exact strings are flagged; scope maps and the empty object are not matched by this rule. Only jobs are checked, not composite actions.
